calibration.basis: A legible, familiar repair intake has a coherent structure and clear labels, but misplaced focus after invalid input weakens recovery. Originality cannot be established beyond the supplied description.

primary_action.input: Keyboard-select Follow-up visit; submit a blank name; enter Avery; preview; append “ I can call before noon.”; return to details and preview again.
primary_action.expected: A focused, editable follow-up note retains the added sentence when reopened.
primary_action.observed: Blank submission focused the invalid name field with an instruction. Preview focused an Avery follow-up note. Back retained Avery and the selected visit, but reopening removed the added sentence.

A-1440.edge_observation: The checked radio and example both reflected Follow-up visit. The example and editor used the same large mint panel. The yellow phone action remained visible in both captured states.
A-1440.fact_check: The page displayed Rowan Chen, 518-555-0142, 15 Example Lane, Albany, and Tuesday–Friday, 8 am–2 pm. The phone link was not activated. These details were not independently verified.
A-1440.strength: The oversized first-sentence panel makes preparing for a personal call the focal task, while the clinician and contact details remain prominent.
A-1440.weakness: Returning to details silently loses edits even when the name and visit do not change.
A-1440.repair: Preserve the edited note across the return-and-preview cycle, including when details remain unchanged.

A-390.edge_observation: The selected radio and example reflected Follow-up visit. The mint example and editor occupied the same panel area. The phone action was visible in both captures at this viewport.
A-390.fact_check: The same clinician, phone, address and hours were displayed. The phone was not dialed; the facts were not independently verified.
A-390.strength: The compact stack keeps the call details, visit choice and note within a clear reading sequence.
A-390.weakness: The quiet loss of an edited sentence undermines the page's promise that the note stays on the page.
A-390.repair: Retain the draft when returning to details and reopening it.

B-1440.weakness: The example's lower position shifts upward when it becomes the editor, making the transition less spatially consistent.
B-1440.repair: Keep the example and editor anchored in a more consistent position while retaining the draft.

B-390.strength: The highlighted visit row makes the choice easy to scan, and the editable call script remains readable on the narrow screen.
B-390.weakness: The editor replaces the form higher in the panel, so its location differs from the example's initial position.
B-390.repair: Improve continuity between the example and editor positions without pushing the call action out of reach.

preference.reason: Both designs make the clinician and call preparation clear, and both recover well from a blank name. B wins because it preserves the user's added sentence at both widths; A silently removes it. B's highlighted selected row also reinforces the visit choice.

unsupported_claims: The displayed contact details and the claim that nothing is sent or booked were not independently verified. No claim is made about behavior after reload, changes to visit details, or actual phone calls.
